primary_references.title: EN 18286:2026 Annex ZA (Table ZA.1): which AI Act requirements the presumption covers
primary_references.url_status: Annex ZA read in the owner's licensed copy of EVS-EN 18286:2026 (PDF pages 50 to 51). The CEN-CENELEC notice does not reproduce it.
primary_references.label: VERIFIED (read in the purchased standard on 2026-10-20)
primary_references.basis: Annex ZA is informative and says conformity with the Table ZA.1 clauses gives a presumption only within the scope of the standard and only from Official Journal citation. Table ZA.1 has 19 rows. Covered: Article 11(1) first sentence (on condition the technical documentation holds all Annex IV items); Article 17(1) first sentence and the first part of the second sentence; Article 17(1)(a) to (m) (point (g) on condition the risk management system complies with Article 9). Not covered: Article 17(2), 17(3), 17(4). No row for Articles 9, 10, 12 to 15, 72 or 73 as such. Eleven clauses are cited in no row: 4.4.2, 8.1.2, 8.3.1.2, 8.4.1, 8.4.3.2, 8.6, 8.9.1, 9.2, 9.6.2.2, 10.1.1.2 and 10.1.2 (own count, confirmed by a text-layer search of the standard; see en18286_text_search). Row remark: applying the standard does not by itself ensure every requirement is met. Warning 1: the presumption lasts only while the Official Journal keeps the reference.
to_verify: Independent check of the clause count and mapping
primary_references.required_action: Keep the label at VERIFIED only for what Annex ZA says; the legal reach of the presumption is a separate question (see presumption_reach).

primary_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
primary_references.url_status: Read in a browser on 2026-10-20 (amending provisions relevant to this register only).

primary_references.basis: Adopted 8 July 2026, OJ L 24.7.2026, in force on the third day after publication. Article 11(1): SMEs, including start-ups, and small mid-caps may give Annex IV in a simplified manner. Article 17(2): proportionality to the size of the provider, in particular SMEs including start-ups and small mid-caps. Article 40(2): the Commission is to request standardisation deliverables to facilitate joint compliance and presumption of conformity with the requirements or obligations in Chapter III, Sections 2 and 3. Article 40(1) is not amended. Chapter III Sections 1 to 3 apply from 2 December 2027 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2 August 2028 for Annex I systems. Article 63(1): SMEs may meet some QMS elements in a simplified manner. Guidelines on Articles 8(2), 9(10) and 17(3) are due by 1 August 2027.

supporting_standards.designation: EVS-EN ISO 9001:2026 (English, PDF, single-user licence) = EN ISO 9001:2026, sixth edition, published 2026-09-16
supporting_standards.role: Comparison baseline in the QMS gap assessment against EN 18286. General, not AI-specific, and gives no presumption of conformity. EN 18286 defines quality as fulfilling regulatory requirements and says this differs from quality in ISO 9001 (definition 3.1.23, Note 2); its own annexes and bibliography cite the 2015 edition of ISO 9001.
supporting_standards.content_read: Full licensed English copy read on screen on 2026-10-20: introduction (also the public ISO sample), scope, clauses 3 to 10, Annex A, bibliography. The protected PDF cannot be text-searched, so the comparison rests on reading, not on an automated search.
planned_use: Delta table: ISO 9001:2026 clause to EN 18286 clause to Article 17(1) point to evidence
Advisory offer wording: QMS gap assessment against EN 18286, with ISO 9001:2026 as a comparison baseline
do_not: Do not claim ISO 9001 certification, conformity or equivalence from owning the standard
Do not describe EN 18286 as building on or extending ISO 9001:2026
Do not share or upload the file (single-user licence)

presumption_reach.label: INFERRED (AI-assisted internal analysis from the texts read on 2026-10-20). OWNER DECISION REQUIRED on customer-facing wording.
points: Article 11 sits in Chapter III, Section 2, so Article 40(1) covers the Article 11(1) row on its words.
Article 17 sits in Section 3. Article 40(1), which Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 did not amend, names Section 2 requirements and Chapter V obligations.

Pointing the other way: Article 16(c) requires a QMS that complies with Article 17; Articles 17(1)(e) and 17(4) refer to harmonised standards; recital 121 treats compliance with harmonised standards as a means to demonstrate conformity; recitals 3 to 5 of Decision 2026/2274 treat EN 18286 as a harmonised standard in support of the Regulation; Annex ZA states a presumption for each Table ZA.1 row; the new Article 40(2) subparagraph refers to presumption of conformity for Sections 2 and 3.
Annex VI point 2 has the provider verify its QMS against Article 17, and Table ZA.1 says applying the standard does not by itself ensure every requirement is met.
presumption_reach.working_position: EN 18286 is cited in the Official Journal and Annex ZA states a presumption for the Table ZA.1 rows within its scope. Do not say that Article 40(1) itself gives a presumption of conformity with Article 17. Do not promise a customer a presumption.

en18286_text_search.label: MEASURED (text-layer search of the owner's EVS online viewer copy of EVS-EN 18286:2026, 56 PDF pages, 55 with text). AI-assisted internal review; not independent validation.
en18286_text_search.method: Page text layers read from the viewer in the owner's browser; term searches and a subclause inventory run on that text; nothing copied out beyond clause numbers and short paraphrases. A term with no hit was re-searched in its split or hyphenated form.
results: Table ZA.1: 19 rows (Article 11(1) first sentence; 17(1) first sentence; 17(1) second sentence first part; 17(1)(a) to (m); 17(2), (3), (4)); 16 covered, 3 not covered; clause lists and conditions match this register.

Articles in Table ZA.1: only 11(1) and 17. Article 9 appears in the point (g) condition and in 4.4.2; Articles 10 and 12 only in 4.4.2; Article 73 only in notes to 7.3.2 and 9.6.1; Article 72 nowhere in the standard.

Subclauses of clauses 4 to 10 with no Table ZA.1 row: 11 of 83 leaf subclauses (4.4.2, 8.1.2, 8.3.1.2, 8.4.1, 8.4.3.2, 8.6, 8.9.1, 9.2, 9.6.2.2, 10.1.1.2, 10.1.2), a cited parent counting for its children.
ISO 9001:2026 is not cited anywhere; Annex B and bibliography item 3 cite EN ISO 9001:2015; item 11 cites EN ISO 9000:2015; Annex C and item 4 cite EN ISO/IEC 42001:2026.

Definition 3.1.23 (quality as fulfilling regulatory requirements; Note 2: differs from quality in EN ISO 9001), 3.4.5 (probability and severity of harm) and 3.2.8 (serious incident per Article 3(49)) read as recorded here.
Supporting standards EN 18228, EN 18284, EN 18229-1, EN 18229-2 and EN ISO/IEC 24970 are cited and footnoted as under preparation.

9.6.1 reporting limits of 2, 10 and 15 days from awareness; 7.1 d) security-of-supply measures; 8.7 unique reference; 9.1 unique identification; 9.7.2.2 notice to market surveillance authorities; 9.5.3 AI system logging: all present as recorded.
